details.description: Grok 4.20 Reasoning is the id xAI's docs list for its Grok 4.20 model, one of several aliases (including grok-4.20-reasoning-latest, grok-4.20-reasoning-gv2 and grok-4.20-beta) that all map to the same underlying build, grok-4.20-0309-reasoning, per xAI's model-alias table. Released April 7, 2026 per xAI's system card, it is a reasoning-focused chat model that accepts text and image input and produces text output over a 1,000,000-token context window. xAI describes it as a general-purpose assistant for question answering, reasoning, research, writing, coding, translation, creative ideation and multimodal reasoning, not intended for high-risk autonomous use in medicine, law, finance or safety-critical systems without human oversight; xAI documents a separate multi-agent deployment of Grok 4.20 under its own grok-4.20-multi-agent id family, distinct from this reasoning id. Artificial Analysis lists this build as deprecated, recommending xAI's newer Grok 4.3 instead.
advantages: Records a 0.00 violation rate on xAI's internal chat-refusal safety evaluation, per its system card (Table 1).
Supports major languages including English, Chinese, Arabic, Hindi and Spanish, plus several dozen others with varying capability, per xAI's system card.
Scores 26 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.
disadvantages: Artificial Analysis marks this build deprecated and recommends xAI's newer Grok 4.3 (high) instead.
Time to first token was 21.53 seconds on Artificial Analysis' benchmark, well above typical models.
Violation rate rises to 0.30 on the AgentHarm agentic-refusal evaluation, versus 0.00 on plain chat refusals, per the system card.
Not designed for high-risk applications such as autonomous medical, legal, financial or safety-critical decisions without human oversight, per xAI's system card.
use_cases: General-purpose assistant tasks: question answering, reasoning, research and writing
Creative ideation and multimodal reasoning over text and images

notes: This id (grok-4.20-reasoning) is one of many aliases -- xAI's own alias table (fetched from the grok-4.20-reasoning-gv2 docs page) lists grok-4.20-reasoning, grok-4.20-reasoning-latest, grok-4.20-reasoning-gv2, grok-4.20, grok-4.20-0309, grok-4.20-beta and several beta/experimental variants -- that all resolve to the same underlying build, grok-4.20-0309-reasoning; this write-up describes that shared model. Artificial Analysis' own page for this model states a 2.0M-token context window, conflicting with both the catalog's 1,000,000 figure and xAI's own docs (also 1,000,000); the catalog/maker value was kept per instructions and the AA figure was not used. Artificial Analysis' output-speed and time-to-first-token numbers fluctuate over time (speed 101.1-106.2 tokens/sec on two later fetches, TTFT a consistent 21.53s on two later fetches); the TTFT figure was corrected from 20.62s to 21.53s to match. VERIFICATION: the description and advantages/use_cases previously claimed this id 'is offered in a single-agent mode and a multi-agent mode' -- this is not supported by this id's own docs page, which never mentions multi-agent mode and lists an alias table containing only reasoning-family ids (no grok-4.20-multi-agent ids). Multi-agent mode is documented xAI-side only under the separate grok-4.20-multi-agent-0309 id family with its own, disjoint alias table; the multi-agent-mode claims here were describing that sibling model, not this one, and have been removed/rescoped. No separate max_output_tokens limit distinct from the 1M context window could be confirmed on any maker page. The system card's CBRN/cybersecurity dual-use capability scores (Table 4) were deliberately excluded as inappropriate to present as selling points.
